an6.46:1.2: At one time Venerable Mahācunda was staying in the land of the Cetis at Sahajāti.
an6.46:2.1: “Take a case where bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles rebuke bhikkhus who practice meditation:
an6.46:2.2: ‘They say, “We practice meditation meditation! We practice meditation meditation!” And they meditate and concentrate and contemplate and ruminate.
an6.46:2.3: Why do they practice meditation meditation? In what way do they practice meditation meditation? How do they practice meditation meditation?’
an6.46:2.4: In this case the bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles are not inspired, and the bhikkhus who practice meditation are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
an6.46:3.1: Now, take a case where bhikkhus who practice meditation meditation rebuke bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles:
an6.46:3.2: ‘They say, “We practice discernment of principles! We practice discernment of principles!” But they’re restless, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, loose-tongued, unmindful, lacking comprehension and concentration, with straying minds and undisciplined faculties.
an6.46:3.3: Why do they practice discernment of principles? In what way do they practice discernment of principles? How do they practice discernment of principles?’
an6.46:3.4: In this case the bhikkhus who practice meditation are not inspired, and the bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
an6.46:4.1: Now, take a case where bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles praise only others like them, not bhikkhus who practice meditation.
an6.46:4.2: In this case the bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles are not inspired, and the bhikkhus who practice meditation are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
an6.46:5.1: And take a case where bhikkhus who practice meditation praise only others like them, not bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles.
an6.46:5.2: In this case the bhikkhus who practice meditation are not inspired, and the bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles are not inspired. And they’re not acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
an6.46:6.1: So you should train like this:
an6.46:6.2: ‘As bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles, we will praise bhikkhus who practice meditation.’
an6.46:6.5: Because it’s rare to find such incredible individuals in the world who have direct meditative experience of the element free of death.
an6.46:7.1: So you should train like this:
an6.46:7.2: ‘As bhikkhus who practice meditation, we will praise bhikkhus who practice discernment of principles.’
an6.46:7.5: Because it’s incredibly rare to find individuals in the world who see the meaning of a deep saying with penetrating wisdom.”
